# Test fixtures

Small, benign, synthetic documents in every format Arca can preview. They are the "real
files" of the test suite: produced by real office software (LibreOffice 24.2, python-pptx),
not by Arca's own writers, so the parsers are exercised on layouts they did not author.

| Files | What they are |
|---|---|
| `report.doc` `.docx` `.odt` `.rtf` `.pdf` `.txt` | the same report: headings, bullet and numbered lists, a table with merged cells, Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew and emoji text |
| `sheet.xls` `.xlsx` `.ods` `.csv` | a sales sheet with formulas, dates, a percentage, a hidden sheet and Cyrillic text (the cached formula results in these LibreOffice-made copies are errors; the viewer shows what is stored) |
| `slides.ppt` `.pptx` `.odp` `slides-impress.pdf` | two slides with bullets, a text box and speaker notes |
| `deck-rich.ppt` `.pptx` | title/bullets/links/table/picture slides, a hidden slide, notes |
| `charts.pptx` | two slides with eight charts: columns (clustered, stacked, percent, negative values, fixed axis), bars, lines (markers, smooth, a gap), stacked areas, a pie and a doughnut; the values are cached in the chart parts as PowerPoint writes them |
| `formulas.xlsx` | a workbook as a library writes it (`tools/fixtures/make_formulas.py`, openpyxl): formulas and **no stored results**, so the viewer has to calculate them; one formula (`TODAY()`) cannot be and must stay text |
| `nested.doc` | Word 97: a table with a table inside one cell, and a two-level numbered list (`tools/fixtures/make_nested.py` + LibreOffice) |
| `body.rtf` `body.rtf.lzfu` | a 29 kB RTF body in Windows-1251 escapes and the same compressed (RTF-LZ "LZFu", as in Outlook messages) by the independent `compressed_rtf` Python package — the oracle for the decompressor |
| `drawing.vsdx` | a Visio drawing with two pages (one a background page), shapes with text and fields, shape data, a hyperlink, a group, a picture and connectors. **Hand-assembled from the VSDX schema** by `tools/fixtures/make_visio.py` — there is no Visio, and LibreOffice cannot export VSDX — so unlike the others it was not made by real software |
| `lo-rich.doc` `lo-latin.doc` | Word 97 files: `lo-rich.doc` has styles, a table, hidden text, tracked changes, footnotes and endnotes, a comment, a hyperlink and a frame; `lo-latin.doc` is Windows-1252 text (curly quotes, euro sign, ellipsis) |
| `enc-agile.docx` `.xlsx`, `enc-standard.docx` | `report.docx` / `sheet.xlsx` password-protected (`tools/fixtures/make_encrypted.py`): agile by `msoffcrypto-tool`, standard (Office 2007) built by the script and cross-checked with `msoffcrypto`'s reader. Passwords: `пароль-123`, `s3cret`, `Password1234_` |
| `enc-rc4-40.pdf` `enc-rc4-128.pdf` `enc-aes-128.pdf` `enc-aes-256.pdf` `enc-open.pdf` | `report.pdf` encrypted by `pikepdf`/qpdf (`tools/fixtures/make_encrypted_pdf.py`). User passwords: `user-40`, `user-128`, `pässword`, `user-256`; `enc-open.pdf` has an empty user password (protected against editing only) |
| `access-2000.mdb` `access-2016.accdb` + `.dump` | Access databases written by **Jackcess** (an independent implementation of the format; `tools/fixtures/access/MakeAccess.java`): customers with memo text of every size (inline, on one page, on several), hyperlinks and Cyrillic/CJK names; orders with 34 rows deleted; one table with a column of every type, nulls and extremes. The `.dump` next to each is what Jackcess reads from it (`DumpDb.java`): typed canonical tokens, compared with the reader's own by `access::tests` |
| `relations-northwind.mdb` | An Access 2000 database written by **Jackcess** (`tools/fixtures/access/MakeRelations.java`): fifteen tables and fifteen relationships of every kind that matters for the relationship diagram (three foreign keys into one table, a two-column key, a table related to itself, two relationships between one pair of tables, a junction table, a one-to-one relationship, cascade flags, a table of 40 columns with no relationship). `access::er::tests` checks that each relationship joins its own two tables, that the "1" is at the parent and the "∞" at the child, that no box overlaps another and that no line crosses a box |

There is no binary Visio (`.vsd`) file here: the real ones used to check the reader (three files from the Apache POI test set, Apache-2.0) are not committed; `vsd::tests` builds drawings from the structure instead, plus one real compressed stream, and `ARCA_VSD_DIR` points the reader's test at real files.

**There is no malware here**, and none belongs here: a real sample must never be committed
(`/corpus/` is ignored by Git for that reason). Hostile inputs are generated by the tests
themselves (mutations, bombs, truncations) or supplied locally through `ARCA_CORPUS_DIR`.

Sources of the generated ones are in `tools/fixtures/`. How they are used:

    ARCA_CORPUS_DIR=$PWD/tests/fixtures cargo test --release -p arca-guest-xray --test e2e_sandbox
    ARCA_CORPUS_DIR=$PWD/tests/fixtures ARCA_GUEST_WASM=... android/host-test/run.sh

Use an absolute path (`$PWD/...`): `cargo test` runs from the crate's directory, so a relative
one does not resolve.
